title: Anterior STEMI
briefing: Severe central chest discomfort for one hour, radiating to jaw and both arms, with nausea and diaphoresis.
history:

Presenting Complaint: 
62-year-old male
Severe chest pain 

History of Presenting Complaint
Central chest discomfort for 1 hour constantly
Onset while at rest watching TV
Radiation to jaw and both arms
Feels like someone pushing down on his chest
Nausea, diaphoresis, “feels like something is wrong”

Relevant Additional History (if asked) 
Experiencing “heartburn” on exertion last few weeks 
Worse on exertion – walking up hill to his office, while walking dog etc
Father had MI in 50s, older brother had CABG a few years ago 

PMH 
Pre-diabetic
Hypertension
Ex-smoker (stopped 40 years ago, limited pack year history <5)

Medications 
Ramipril

Allergies 
NKDA

Social History 
Works in construction – office job, no HGV driving 
Usually fit and active, walks dog for miles per day
preparation: 20-minute simulation and 20-minute debrief. Prepare actor/mannequin, monitor and locally reviewed investigation assets. Equipment details need faculty review.

objectives.text: Perform a structured history and A-E assessment
Interpret investigations and form a differential
Communicate diagnosis and plan using SBAR

stages.name: History and A-E Assessment
stages.cues:
Sim LeaderProvide history chest pain and progressive shortness of breath
If prompted provide PMHx of HTN, pre-diabetes, cardiac FHx

Sim Nurse
Prompt learner to consider analgesia
Provide ECG only after complete history taking
stages.sourceTrigger: structured history and A-E completed, ECG provided, time elapsed

actions.text: Introduce self and confirm patient identity
Systematic history including SOCRATES for chest pain

stages.name: Differential Diagnosis/Investigations
stages.findings: As above; elevated HR, down-trending BP.
stages.cues:
Sim LeaderPatient to complain of pain and nausea
BP down-trending, HR increasing
Query diagnosis - “Am I going to die?”

Sim Nurse
Provide ECG when requested
Prompt learner with patient discomfort
Prompt learner for anti-emetic if sick
Ask for most likely diagnosis/differential
stages.sourceTrigger: Identifies ACS, appropriate treatment prescribed, differential given, escalation, time elapsed

actions.text: Prescribe analgesia/anti-emetic if not done already

stages.name: Patient Deterioration
stages.findings: Tachycardia, hypoxia, hypotension. Visibly breathless with bibasal crackles.
stages.cues:
Sim LeaderEscalate hypoxia and tachycardia
Reduce blood pressure
Patient to become increasingly distressed
Drop sats to 70s if O2 not commenced

Sim Nurse
Prompt learner to recognise patient deterioration
Provide CXR when requested
Provide ABG when requested
If 2222 not called or alternative help sought – prompt learner that seems to be time critical emergency
stages.sourceTrigger: CXR requested, repeat A-E assessment underway, time elapsed, calls for senior support/2222

stages.name: Deterioration, Escalation, SBAR Handover
stages.findings: Less breathless, normal sats on O2, ongoing bibasal crackles, HR and BP improving.
stages.cues:
Sim LeaderTake on role of medical registrar arriving
Receive SBAR handover
Prompt for differential diagnosis
Prompt for any missed investigations/interpretation


Sim Nurse
Reassure patient/acting in background

actions.text: Identifies acute pulmonary oedema on CXR

review: Rhythms, timers, transition combinations and treatment responses unset

title: Tension pneumothorax
briefing: Abrupt left-sided pleuritic chest pain for two hours, pain 7/10 and shortness of breath.

Presenting Complaint: 
23-year-old male
Severe chest pain 

History of Presenting Complaint
Sudden onset pain 2 hours ago
Sharp and left sided with no radiation
Worse on inspiration
Tried paracetamol without improvement
Pain 7/10
Worried as now short of breath while talking, walking into ED, climbing stairs

Relevant Additional History (if asked) 
Father had “connective tissue problem” and suddenly died when he was younger
Semi-professional basketball player

PMH 
Nil

Medications 
OTC Paracetamol

Allergies 
NKDA

Social History 
Non-smoker
Works as a PE teacher
Driver
No alcohol
preparation: 20-minute simulation and 20-minute debrief. Prepare actor/mannequin, monitor and locally reviewed investigation assets. Equipment details need faculty review.

objectives.text: Perform a structured history and A-E assessment
Interpret investigations and form a differential
Communicate diagnosis and plan using SBAR

stages.name: A-E ASSESSMENT
stages.findings: Breathless, reduced AE and chest expansion on L side
stages.cues:
Sim LeaderProvide history of acute onset chest pain and shortness of breath
If prompted give family history of ‘connective tissue disorder', non-smoker, nil trauma.

Sim Nurse
Ask for early differential diagnosis 
Prompt learner to consider analgesia
stages.sourceTrigger: completes history and initial A-E, provides differential diagnoses, requests CXR

actions.text: Introduce self and confirm patient identity

stages.name: Differential Diagnosis/Investigations
stages.findings: Mildly breathless, sats stable on O2
stages.cues:
Sim LeaderPatient to complain of discomfort
Asks for diagnosis and plan
Drop sats if no O2 therapy given

Sim Nurse
Provide ECG when asked
Provide ABG when asked
stages.sourceTrigger: Investigations complete/interpretation performed, differential given, time elapsed

stages.name: Patient Deterioration/Escalation
stages.findings: Distressed, R tracheal deviation, no breath sounds on L side
stages.cues:
Sim LeaderEscalate hypoxia and tachycardia, reduce blood pressure (improves to 94% on 15L)
Patient to become increasingly distressed
If students commit to intervention – “Have you done this before doctor?”

Sim Nurse
Prompt learner to recognise patient deterioration
Provide CXR
If 2222 not called or alternative help sought – prompt learner that seems to be time critical emergency
Prepares kit/model for decompression
stages.sourceTrigger: 2222 call put out, repeat A-E assessment underway, commits to decompression, time elapsed

actions.text: Recognises need for immediate needle decompression
Receives CXR – accurately interprets as tension PTX

stages.name: SBAR Handover, intervention
stages.findings: As above, increasing hypoxia and haemodynamic instability. Periarrest.
stages.cues:
Sim LeaderTake on role of medical registrar arriving
Receive SBAR handover and differential
Prompt for any missed investigations/interpretation
Initiates/supervises decompression


Sim Nurse
Reassure patient/acting in background
stages.sourceTrigger: Completed handover and intervention – scenario end

actions.text: Completes needle decompression under supervision of medical registrar

review: Rhythms, timers, transition combinations and treatment responses unset

Presenting Complaint: 
40-year-old female patient
Collapse with palpitations

History of Presenting Complaint
3-day history of increasingly unwell with intermittent palpitations and feeling out of breath/exercise intolerance
Experienced sudden light-headedness and collapsed while out shopping this morning
Witnessed loss of consciousness for ~10-15 seconds
Rapid recovery, no post-ictal confusion
No tongue biting, incontinence or seizure activity

Relevant History (if asked) 
Returned from Australia 10 days ago
Taking combined oral contraceptive pill
Mild pleuritic chest discomfort

PMH 
Migraine

Medications 
Combined oral contraceptive pill
Sumatriptan PRN

Allergies 
NKDA

Social History 
Non-smoker
Lives with husband
